tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

"leipzig-1":{ caption:"Leipzig Hauptbahnhof", blurb:"Reportedly Europe's largest railway station by floor area. It feels it.", alt:"The long sandstone facade of Leipzig Hauptbahnhof seen from across the street, with a yellow and blue tram passing on the right", note:"The station is the size of a small town and has a shopping centre inside it, so every trip into Leipzig started with ten minutes of finding the right way out." },
        "leipzig-2":{ caption:"Down to the S-Bahn", blurb:"A very long staircase and a very clean tunnel.", alt:"Looking down a steep staircase into a white-tiled underground S-Bahn station in Leipzig's city tunnel, with passengers waiting on the platform below", note:"The city tunnel stations are all white tile and straight lines, lit like an operating theatre. Ours at home are not like this, and I took the photo mostly out of envy." },
        "leipzig-3":{ caption:"The university's glass church", blurb:"Half lecture hall, half cathedral, entirely on purpose.", alt:"The Paulinum of Leipzig University on Augustusplatz, a modern glass and stone building shaped like a gothic church front with a rose window", note:"The university built a glass building in the shape of the church that stood here until it was blown up in the sixties. A strange, sharp-edged thing to stand in front of, and I liked it a lot." },
        "leipzig-4":{ caption:"The dark church", blurb:"Neo-gothic, soot-black, and parked in on all sides.", alt:"A tall dark neo-gothic church in Leipzig with twin spires and a large rose window, with cars parked along the street directly in front of it", note:"Black stone, two spires, an enormous rose window — and a row of parked cars pressed right up against the front of it, including a very yellow one. Nobody here seems impressed by their own buildings." },
        "leipzig-5":{ caption:"Bach outside his church", blurb:"He worked here for twenty-seven years. The statue does not look relaxed.", alt:"The Thomaskirche in Leipzig on an overcast day, with the bronze statue of Johann Sebastian Bach on its plinth in the foreground", note:"Bach stands outside the Thomaskirche with one hand behind his back, looking like he is about to tell somebody off about a rehearsal. He was cantor here for twenty-seven years, so he probably had cause." },
        "leipzig-6":{ caption:"Bach's grave", blurb:"A brass slab in the floor with fresh flowers on it.", alt:"The interior of the Thomaskirche looking towards the golden altar, with the bronze grave slab of Johann Sebastian Bach set into the floor in the foreground and flowers laid on it", note:"He is buried in the floor in front of the altar, under a plain brass slab with somebody's fresh flowers on it. Of everything we saw in two weeks, this is the one that actually stopped me." },
        "leipzig-7":{ caption:"Instruments under glass", blurb:"Three hundred years old and still better looking than my guitar.", alt:"A violin and a larger string instrument displayed in a museum vitrine at the Bach museum, with a handwritten music manuscript behind them", note:"A violin and something viola-shaped in a case, with one of Bach's manuscripts behind them — the handwriting is tiny and completely certain. I play guitar badly enough to find that intimidating." },
        "leipzig-8":{ caption:"Kofola in Leipzig", blurb:"Eight hundred kilometres from home and there's a Slovak stall on the market square.", alt:"A hand holding a cup of Kofola in front of a Slovak food stall called Koliba on Leipzig's market square, with a Slovak flag flying above it", note:"We came round the corner of the market and there it was: a Slovak flag, a stall called Koliba, and Kofola on tap. I have never been so pleased to find something I can buy at home for half the price." },
        "leipzig-9":{ caption:"Into the courtyard", blurb:"Every wall in this part of town has something painted on it.", alt:"The graffiti-covered entrance passage to a courtyard in Leipzig, with a scrap-metal sculpture and a hand-painted Mrs. Hippie sign above the gate", note:"A gate with a scrap-metal figure on the roof and Mrs. Hippie painted across it, opening into a yard where nothing has been repainted in thirty years. This is the part of Leipzig I would come back for." },
        "leipzig-10":{ caption:"A wall of records", blurb:"Somebody nailed a record collection to the side of a building.", alt:"Dozens of vinyl records nailed in a cascade across a weathered courtyard wall in Leipzig, with bicycles and information boards below", note:"Dozens of records nailed straight into the plaster, spilling down the wall like water. Nobody was guarding it and nobody had taken any, which says something nice about the neighbourhood." },
        "leipzig-11":{ caption:"The monument, from the far end", blurb:"It doesn't photograph well. It doesn't need to.", alt:"The Monument to the Battle of the Nations in Leipzig silhouetted against the sun at the far end of its long reflecting pool", note:"You see it from the other end of a long pool of water, dead centre, with the sun directly behind it. It looks less like a monument and more like something that landed." },
        "leipzig-12":{ caption:"At the foot of it", blurb:"The people at the bottom are there for scale. They don't help.", alt:"The Monument to the Battle of the Nations seen from its base, with the giant stone archangel above the entrance and tiny figures of people on the plaza below", note:"A hill of stone with an archangel the size of a house over the door, and the people by the entrance look like a mistake in the picture. It is meant to make you feel small and it is very good at its job." },
        "leipzig-13":{ caption:"Inside the dome", blurb:"Four stone giants sitting in the dark, minding the dead.", alt:"The interior hall of the Monument to the Battle of the Nations seen from an upper gallery, with colossal seated stone guardian figures and stained glass windows", note:"From the upper gallery you look down on four colossal seated figures guarding the hall, the stained glass throwing colour across them. Every sound in there takes about four seconds to come back." },
        "leipzig-14":{ caption:"Leipzig from the top", blurb:"Worth every step of the staircase, and there were a lot of steps.", alt:"The view from the top of the Monument to the Battle of the Nations over its reflecting pool towards the Leipzig skyline on a clear day", note:"From the platform you get the whole city at once: the pool below, then trees, then Leipzig going flat all the way to the horizon.         "leipzig-15":{ caption:"After the rain", blurb:"Old factory on one side, new offices on the other, nobody about.", alt:"An empty wet street in Leipzig at dusk, with a long old industrial hall and its steel-framed windows on the left and a pale modern office block on the right", note:"An old factory hall on one side, a new office block on the other, and the wet road between them taking all the light.         "freetime-2":{ caption:"Der Bismarckturm", blurb:"Noch ein Spaziergang, noch ein großes graues Ding am Ende.", alt:"Wir drei stehen an einem sonnigen Nachmittag auf der Wiese vor dem steinernen Bismarckturm bei Schkeuditz", note:"So sahen unsere freien Nachmittage aus: etwas auf der Karte aussuchen, hinlaufen, fotografieren, zurücklaufen.         "leipzig-2":{ caption:"Runter zur S-Bahn", blurb:"Eine sehr lange Treppe und ein sehr sauberer Tunnel.", alt:"Blick eine steile Treppe hinunter in eine weiß geflieste S-Bahn-Station im Leipziger City-Tunnel, unten warten Fahrgäste auf dem Bahnsteig", note:"Die Stationen im City-Tunnel sind alles weiße Fliesen und gerade Linien, beleuchtet wie ein OP-Saal.         "leipzig-3":{ caption:"Die Glaskirche der Uni", blurb:"Halb Hörsaal, halb Kathedrale, und zwar mit Absicht.", alt:"Das Paulinum der Universität Leipzig am Augustusplatz, ein moderner Bau aus Glas und Stein in Form einer gotischen Kirchenfront mit Fensterrose", note:"Die Universität hat ein Gebäude aus Glas in der Form der Kirche gebaut, die hier stand, bis sie in den Sechzigern gesprengt wurde.         "leipzig-4":{ caption:"Die dunkle Kirche", blurb:"Neogotisch, rußschwarz und von allen Seiten zugeparkt.", alt:"Eine hohe dunkle neogotische Kirche in Leipzig mit zwei Türmen und großer Fensterrose, davor parkende Autos direkt an der Straße", note:"Schwarzer Stein, zwei Türme, eine riesige Fensterrose — und direkt davor eine Reihe parkender Autos, darunter ein sehr gelbes.         "leipzig-5":{ caption:"Bach vor seiner Kirche", blurb:"Siebenundzwanzig Jahre hat er hier gearbeitet.         "leipzig-6":{ caption:"Bachs Grab", blurb:"Eine Bronzeplatte im Boden, mit frischen Blumen darauf.", alt:"Der Innenraum der Thomaskirche mit Blick zum goldenen Altar, im Vordergrund die bronzene Grabplatte von Johann Sebastian Bach im Boden, darauf liegen Blumen", note:"Er liegt im Boden vor dem Altar, unter einer schlichten Bronzeplatte, auf der frische Blumen von irgendjemandem liegen.         "leipzig-7":{ caption:"Instrumente hinter Glas", blurb:"Dreihundert Jahre alt und immer noch schöner als meine Gitarre.", alt:"Eine Geige und ein größeres Streichinstrument in einer Museumsvitrine im Bach-Museum, dahinter ein handgeschriebenes Notenmanuskript", note:"Eine Geige und etwas Bratschenförmiges in der Vitrine, dahinter eines von Bachs Manuskripten — die Handschrift ist winzig und vollkommen sicher.         "leipzig-8":{ caption:"Kofola in Leipzig", blurb:"Achthundert Kilometer von zu Hause, und auf dem Markt steht ein slowakischer Stand.", alt:"Eine Hand hält einen Becher Kofola vor einem slowakischen Essensstand namens Koliba auf dem Leipziger Markt, darüber weht eine slowakische Flagge", note:"Wir kamen um die Ecke des Marktes, und da war sie: eine slowakische Fahne, ein Stand namens Koliba und Kofola vom Fass.         "leipzig-9":{ caption:"Rein in den Hinterhof", blurb:"In dieser Gegend ist auf jede Wand irgendetwas gemalt.", alt:"Die mit Graffiti bedeckte Durchfahrt zu einem Leipziger Hinterhof, über dem Tor eine Schrottskulptur und ein handgemaltes Mrs.-Hippie-Schild", note:"Ein Tor mit einer Schrottfigur auf dem Dach und Mrs. Hippie quer darüber, dahinter ein Hof, in dem seit dreißig Jahren nichts gestrichen wurde.         "leipzig-10":{ caption:"Eine Wand aus Schallplatten", blurb:"Jemand hat eine Plattensammlung an eine Hauswand genagelt.", alt:"Dutzende Schallplatten in einer Kaskade an eine verwitterte Hinterhofwand in Leipzig genagelt, darunter Fahrräder und Infotafeln", note:"Dutzende Platten direkt in den Putz genagelt, die Wand hinunterlaufend wie Wasser.         "leipzig-11":{ caption:"Das Denkmal, vom anderen Ende", blurb:"Es fotografiert sich schlecht.         "leipzig-12":{ caption:"Ganz unten davor", blurb:"Die Leute unten sind der Maßstab.         "leipzig-13":{ caption:"Unter der Kuppel", blurb:"Vier steinerne Riesen sitzen im Dunkeln und bewachen die Toten.", alt:"Die Ruhmeshalle des Völkerschlachtdenkmals von einer oberen Galerie aus gesehen, mit kolossalen sitzenden Wächterfiguren aus Stein und bunten Glasfenstern", note:"Von der oberen Galerie schaut man auf vier kolossale sitzende Figuren hinunter, die die Halle bewachen, während die Glasfenster Farbe über sie werfen.         "leipzig-12":{ caption:"Priamo pod ním", blurb:"Ľudia dole sú tam pre mierku.         "leipzig-13":{ caption:"Pod kupolou", blurb:"Štyria kamenní obri sedia v tme a strážia mŕtvych.", alt:"Sieň slávy pamätníka bitky národov z hornej galérie, s kolosálnymi sediacimi kamennými strážcami a vitrážovými oknami", note:"Z hornej galérie sa pozeráš dole na štyri kolosálne sediace postavy, ktoré strážia sieň, a vitráže po nich hádžu farbu.         "leipzig-14":{ caption:"Lipsko zhora", blurb:"Stálo to za každý schod, a schodov bolo dosť.", alt:"Výhľad z vrcholu pamätníka bitky národov cez vodný bazén na panorámu Lipska v jasný deň", note:"Z plošiny máš celé mesto naraz: dole bazén, potom stromy a potom Lipsko naploho až po horizont.         "leipzig-15":{ caption:"Po daždi", blurb:"Stará fabrika na jednej strane, nové kancelárie na druhej, nikde nikto.", alt:"Prázdna mokrá ulica v Lipsku za súmraku, vľavo dlhá stará priemyselná hala s oceľovými oknami, vpravo svetlá moderná kancelárska budova", note:"Stará fabrická hala na jednej strane, nová kancelárska budova na druhej a medzi nimi mokrá cesta, ktorá pohltí všetko svetlo.         "dresden-1":{ caption:"Labe z mosta", blurb:"Prvý pohľad na Drážďany: veľmi modrá obloha a rieka plná lodí.", alt:"Rieka Labe z drážďanského mosta, vpravo zakotvené kolesové parníky pri brehu a za nimi sklenená kupola akadémie umení", note:"Prešli sme cez most a celé mesto sa zjavilo naraz — rieka, terasa, parníky vyrovnané pri brehu.         "dresden-2":{ caption:"Poľská koruna", blurb:"Brána so zlatou korunou navrchu, lebo jedno kráľovstvo nestačilo.", alt:"Brána Kronentor drážďanského Zwingeru so zlátenou poľskou korunou, pohľad z príjazdovej cesty", note:"Brána do Zwingeru nesie zlatú poľskú korunu, pretože August Silný vládol Sasku aj Poľsku naraz a chcel, aby to každý príchodzí vedel. O zdržanlivosť tu nešlo." },
        "dresden-3":{ caption:"Fontána pri Zwingeri", blurb:"Jeden prúd vody, jazierko a prvé poriadne jesenné lístie.", alt:"Jediný prúd fontány v jazierku pri Zwingeri, za ním na vyvýšenine pavilón Zwingeru, v popredí spadnuté jesenné lístie na tráve", note:"Jazierko, jeden veľmi odhodlaný prúd vody a Zwinger na brehu za ním.         "dresden-4":{ caption:"Hofkirche", blurb:"Fotené zdola, lebo inak sa to do záberu nezmestí.", alt:"Barokový katolícky dvorný kostol Hofkirche v Drážďanoch pohľadom zdola od schodov, s vysokou vežou, sochami pozdĺž strechy a skupinou ľudí pri vchode", note:"Keď stojíš dole pri schodoch, celý kostol sa ti do mobilu nezmestí, takže máš toto: portál, sochy a vežu, ktorá uteká von zo záberu. cd /c/Users/16/Desktop/website
# ids declared in GALLERY_STRUCTURE
sed -n '/const GALLERY_STRUCTURE/,/^  };/p' index.html | grep -o '"[a-z0-9]*-[0-9]*"' | tr -d '"' | sort -u > /tmp/gs.txt
sed -n '/IMAGES:START/,/IMAGES:END/p' index.html | grep -o '"[a-z0-9]*-[0-9]*":' | tr -d '":' | sort -u > /tmp/img.txt
sed -n '/const PHOTO_META/,/^  };/p' index.html | grep -o '"[a-z0-9]*-[0-9]*":' | tr -d '":' | sort -u > /tmp/pm.txt
echo "GALLERY_STRUCTURE: $(wc -l < /tmp/gs.txt)   IMAGES: $(wc -l < /tmp/img.txt)   PHOTO_META: $(wc -l < /tmp/pm.txt)"
echo "--- in GALLERY_STRUCTURE but missing from IMAGES ---"; comm -23 /tmp/gs.txt /tmp/img.txt
echo "--- in GALLERY_STRUCTURE but missing from PHOTO_META ---"; comm -23 /tmp/gs.txt /tmp/pm.txt
echo "--- in IMAGES but not in any gallery ---"; comm -13 /tmp/gs.txt /tmp/img.txt
for l in en de sk; do
  awk -v L="$l" '$0 ~ "^    "L": [{]" {f=1} f && /^    [}],?$/ {f=0} f' index.html | grep -o '"[a-z0-9]*-[0-9]*":{' | tr -d '":{' | sort -u > /tmp/cap_$l.txt
  echo "$l captions: $(wc -l < /tmp/cap_$l.txt)  missing vs galleries: $(comm -23 /tmp/gs.txt /tmp/cap_$l.txt | tr '\n' ' ')"
done

input.new_string:

  dropped in favour of `data/`. Kept only in case the embedding is ever wanted again.
  (Also: this dev machine has only the Microsoft Store Python stub — `python3` and `node`
  both resolve to nothing — so neither could run here anyway.)

content.text: Now the gotcha that my change made actively wrong:

input.old_string:
- `.img-el` sizing lives on the `` itself (`max-width`/`max-height`/`aspect-ratio`, `width:auto;height:auto`), not on the `.img-wrap` div around it. A plain `
` with its own `aspect-ratio` can render wider than its flex parent and overflow the postcard border on narrow phones; a replaced element like `` can't. Don't move sizing onto `.img-wrap`.
input.new_string:
- `.img-el` sizing lives on the `` itself, not on the `.img-wrap` div around it. A plain `
` with its own `aspect-ratio` can render wider than its flex parent and overflow the postcard border on narrow phones; a replaced element like `` can't. Don't move sizing onto `.img-wrap`. - **How the photo is sized** (this replaced an earlier `width:auto;height:auto` + `max-width`/`max-height` + fixed `aspect-ratio:3/2` + `object-fit:cover` setup — don't reinstate any part of that without reading this): - There is **no fixed aspect-ratio and no `cover`**. The photos are a mix of portrait (3:4), landscape (4:3) and square; a 3:2 centre-crop cut the top and bottom off every portrait one, heads included. `object-fit:contain` + the real ratio means nothing is cropped. - The ratio arrives as a CSS custom property `--ar`, set inline per photo by `showImage()` from `PHOTO_META`'s `w`/`h`, with a `1.5` fallback for empty slots. - The width is `min(66vw, 760px, calc(min(64vh,600px) * var(--ar)))`. The third term is the height cap expressed as a width, which is what keeps the photo inside *both* caps. **`max-width`/`max-height` cannot do this job any more:** they only preserve an image's proportions while width and height are `auto`, and an `auto`-sized `` that hasn't loaded has no intrinsic size — so the card would collapse to nothing until the file arrived, and stay collapsed if it 404'd. Photos are separate files now, so that is a real request, not bytes already in the page. Giving width and height explicitly instead would make `max-*` clamp each axis independently and distort the box (observed: 760×461 for a photo that should be 346×461). - A portrait photo makes a portrait card, and the postcard's divided back can't run two columns side by side in one — they get too narrow to read. `showImage()` adds `.is-portrait` to `.image-frame` when `w < h`, and the back stacks instead. This case didn't exist while everything was cropped to 3:2 landscape.

## Running the converter

```
pip install pillow --break-system-packages
python3 converter.py --html index.html --manifest manifest.json
```

`manifest.json`: `{ "photo-id": "path/to/source/photo.jpg" }` — ids must already exist in
`GALLERY_STRUCTURE`/`IMAGES` (add them there first if new). Unknown ids are skipped with a
stderr warning, not silently dropped or crashed on. The script reports each photo's
encoded size and a running total; treat >15MB combined as the signal to lower
`MAX_DIMENSION` / `JPEG_QUALITY` at the top of `converter.py`, not to switch approach.
input.new_string:
## Adding a photo

No tooling involved any more — it's four edits, all by hand:

1. Drop the file into the right `data/<Gallery>/` folder. Keep it webp and roughly
   1000–1300px on the long edge; the display caps are 760×600 CSS px, so anything much
   larger is wasted bytes.
2. Add its id to `GALLERY_STRUCTURE` in the position you want it shown.
3. Add an `IMAGES` entry with the path (exact case), and a `PHOTO_META` entry with the
   file's real `w`/`h` — without those the card is the wrong shape until the file loads.
4. Add a `captions` entry in **all three** `I18N` blocks.

Ids must exist in all four structures or the gallery will render a fallback with the raw
id as its caption.
